title: Appledore Soup
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- 3 potatoes
- 1 quart milk
- 2 slices onion
- 3 tablespoons butter
- 2 tablespoons flour
- 1½ teaspoons salt
- ¼ teaspoon celery salt
- ⅛ teaspoon pepper
- Few grains cayenne
- 1 teaspoon chopped parsley
- 3 tablespoons tomato catsup

## Directions

1. Cook potatoes in boiling salted water; when soft, rub through a strainer.
2. Scald milk with onion, remove onion, and add milk slowly to potatoes.
3. Melt half the butter, add dry ingredients, stir until well mixed, then stir into boiling soup; cook one minute, strain, add remaining butter, and sprinkle with parsley.
4. Add three tablespoons tomato catsup just before serving.

title: Asparagus on Toast
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- Boiled Asparagus
- Buttered Toast or Milk Toast

## Directions

1. Serve Boiled Asparagus on Buttered or Milk Toast

title: Baked Macaroni with Cheese
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- 3/4 cup macaroni
- 2 quarts boiling water
- 1 tablespoon salt
- grated cheese
- 1 1/2 cups White Sauce
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 2 tablespoons flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1 1/2 cups scalded milk
- buttered crumbs

## Directions

1. Cook macaroni in boiling salted water twenty minutes or until soft
2. Drain in strainer
3. Pour over it cold water to prevent pieces from adhering
4. Put a layer of boiled macaroni in buttered baking dish
5. Sprinkle with grated cheese
6. Repeat
7. Pour over White Sauce
8. Cover with buttered crumbs
9. Bake until crumbs are brown

title: Buttered Eggs with Tomatoes
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- tomatoes
- salt
- pepper
- flour
- butter

## Directions

1. Cut tomatoes in one-third inch slices.
2. Sprinkle with salt and pepper, dredge with flour, and sauté in butter.
3. Serve a buttered egg on each slice of tomato.

title: Celery Soup I
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- 3 cups celery (cut in one-half inch pieces)
- 1 pint boiling water
- 2½ cups milk
- 1 slice onion
- 3 tablespoons butter
- ¼ cup flour
- Salt and pepper

## Directions

1. Wash and scrape celery before cutting in pieces, cook in boiling water until soft, and rub through a sieve.
2. Scald milk with the onion, remove onion, and add milk to celery.
3. Bind with butter and flour cooked together.
4. Season with salt and pepper.
5. Outer and old stalks of celery may be utilized for soups.
6. Serve with croûtons, crisp crackers, or pulled bread.

title: Chicken Stew
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- a fowl
- boiling water
- one-half tablespoon salt
- one-eighth teaspoon pepper
- one-third cup flour
- cold water
- butter

## Directions

1. Dress, clean, and cut up a fowl.
2. Put in a stewpan, cover with boiling water, and cook slowly until tender, adding one-half tablespoon salt and one-eighth teaspoon pepper when fowl is about half cooked.
3. Thicken stock with one-third cup flour diluted with enough cold water to pour easily.
4. Serve with Dumplings, adding butter if desired richer.

title: Chicken Timbales II
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- 2 tablespoons butter
- ¼ cup stale bread crumbs
- ⅔ cup milk
- 1 cup chopped cooked chicken
- ½ tablespoon chopped parsley
- 2 eggs
- Salt
- Pepper

## Directions

1. Melt butter, add bread crumbs and milk, and cook five minutes, stirring constantly.
2. Add chicken, parsley, and eggs slightly beaten.
3. Season with salt and pepper.
4. Turn into buttered individual moulds, having moulds two-thirds full set in pan of hot water, cover with buttered paper, and bake twenty minutes.
5. Serve with Béchamel Sauce.

title: Corn Fritters
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- one can corn
- one cup flour
- one teaspoon baking powder
- two teaspoons salt
- one-fourth teaspoon paprika
- two eggs
- fresh hot lard

## Directions

1. Chop corn.
2. Mix and sift dry ingredients.
3. Add yolks of eggs beaten until thick.
4. Fold in whites of eggs beaten stiff.
5. Cook in a frying-pan in fresh hot lard.
6. Drain on paper.

title: Cream of Tomato Soup
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- ½ can tomatoes
- 2 teaspoons sugar
- ¼ teaspoon soda
- 1 quart milk
- 1 slice onion
- 4 tablespoons flour
- 1 teaspoon salt
- ⅛ teaspoon pepper
- ⅓ cup butter

## Directions

1. Scald milk with onion, remove onion, and thicken milk with flour diluted with cold water until thin enough to pour, being careful that the mixture is free from lumps; cook twenty minutes, stirring constantly at first.
2. Cook tomatoes with sugar fifteen minutes, add soda, and rub through a sieve; combine mixtures, and strain into tureen over butter, salt, and pepper.

title: Dropped Eggs (Poached)
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- eggs
- boiling salted water
- salt
- butter
- muffin rings
- buttered toast
- parsley

## Directions

1. Have ready a shallow pan two-thirds full of boiling salted water, allowing one-half tablespoon salt to one quart of water.
2. Put two or three buttered muffin rings in the water.
3. Break each egg separately into a cup, and carefully slip into a muffin ring.
4. The water should cover the eggs.
5. When there is a film over the top, and the white is firm, carefully remove with a buttered skimmer to circular pieces of buttered toast, and let each person season his own egg with butter, salt, and pepper.
6. If cooked for an invalid, garnish with four toast points and a bit of parsley.

title: Leek and Potato Soup
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- 1 bunch leeks
- 1 cup celery
- 2½ tablespoons butter
- 1 quart milk
- 2½ cups potatoes
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 2 tablespoons flour
- Salt and pepper
- Cayenne

## Directions

1. Cut leeks and celery in very thin slices crosswise and cook in two and one-half tablespoons butter, stirring constantly, ten minutes.
2. Add milk, and cook in double boiler forty minutes.
3. Cut potatoes in slices and cut slices in small pieces; then cook in boiling salted water ten minutes.
4. Melt two tablespoons butter, add flour, milk with vegetables and potatoes.
5. Cook until potatoes are soft, and season with salt, pepper, and cayenne.

title: Macaroni, Italian Style
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- 1 cup macaroni
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 2 tablespoons flour
- 1 1/2 cups scalded milk
- 2/3 cup grated cheese
- salt and paprika
- 1/4 cup finely chopped cold boiled ham

## Directions

1. Break macaroni in one-inch pieces
2. Cook in boiling salted water
3. Drain
4. Reheat in sauce made of butter, flour, and milk
5. Add cheese to sauce
6. As soon as cheese is melted, season with salt and paprika
7. Turn on to a serving dish
8. Sprinkle with ham
9. Garnish with parsley

title: Macaroni with White Sauce
attribution: Fannie Merritt Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896).
text:
## Ingredients

- 3/4 cup macaroni broken in inch pieces
- 2 quarts boiling water
- 1 tablespoon salt
- 1 1/2 cups White Sauce
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 2 tablespoons flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1 1/2 cups scalded milk

## Directions

1. Cook macaroni in boiling salted water twenty minutes or until soft
2. Drain in strainer
3. Pour over it cold water to prevent pieces from adhering
4. Reheat in White Sauce
5. For White Sauce: Melt two tablespoons butter
6. Add two tablespoons flour with one-half teaspoon salt
7. Pour on slowly one and one-half cups scalded milk
